Instructions for Database Entity & DbContext Initialization
Context
You are a Senior .NET Backend Developer. I have a completed ERD for a laptop e-commerce project called "999 Laptop". Your task is to implement the Code-First approach using Entity Framework Core.

Core Database Schema Requirements
Users Table:

UserID (int, PK, Identity).

Username (varchar, 5-10 chars, regex: ^[a-z0-9]+$).

PasswordHash (string, required).

Role (default: "Customer").

Product System:

Products: Main table containing common fields (ProductID, ProductName, BrandID, CategoryID, BasePrice, StockQuantity, ProductImage, Status).

ProductDetails: Contains laptop-specific specs (CPU, RAM, GPU, Display, Storage, Battery, Weight, OS).

Brands & Categories: Standard lookup tables. Categories must support hierarchical structure via ParentID.

Relationships (Crucial):

Products & ProductDetails: One-to-One (1:1) relationship. ProductDetails.ProductID is both PK and FK.

Products & (Brands/Categories): Many-to-One.

Orders & OrderDetails: Header-Detail pattern. IMPORTANT: OrderDetails must store the UnitPrice at the time of purchase to prevent historical data loss if product prices change.

Cart, Wishlist, & Reviews: Junction tables linking Users and Products. Cart must include Quantity.

Implementation Rules
Model Definitions:

Use Data Annotations (e.g., [Key], [Required], [StringLength]) for simple constraints.

Use Fluent API in OnModelCreating for complex relationships (especially the 1:1 Product-ProductDetails and Delete behaviors).

Navigation Properties: All navigation properties (Collections and Reference objects) must be marked as virtual to support Lazy Loading if needed.

Naming Convention: Use PascalCase for C# properties and ensure they match the English names provided in the ERD.

Architecture: * Keep Entities clean (POCO classes).

Configurations should be moved to separate EntityTypeConfiguration classes if the OnModelCreating becomes too crowded.
